comment: Divergence ledger, read by the unified corpus gate (corpus_gate). Both
channels gate commits. An entry masks nothing silently: it pins where and
how much a case may diverge on a channel, and it fails the gate when stale (a
divergence that no longer exceeds the tier floor, or a scope that never
matched). Envelopes are per-case, per-channel, per-scope measured facts with
a mandatory cause and source, never a tolerance: the tier floors of the test
harness are untouched and unreachable from here. Every add, widen or flip
lands as a population-lock diff. Kinds: 'divergence' (field-granular

causes.fpc-delphi-ulp: Last-ulp libm differences between the Delphi build of r4133 and the FPC build of dss_capi 0.14.5, amplified through the solve. This engine matches dss_capi 0.14.5 exactly (the capi_v0145 channel is bit-clean), while r4133 settles a near-identical state a few ulp away. Same class as the proven dSpeed cancellation floor: a floor between the two OpenDSS builds, not a bug of this engine.
causes.iteration-count-delta: Solve and control fixpoint iteration counts that differ from r4133: last-ulp rounding between the Delphi and FPC builds shifts convergence-check outcomes, and the GenDispatcher dispatch iterates differently. This engine matches the exact count of dss_capi 0.14.5 on capi_v0145, and on r4133 the state is near-identical in a different iteration count. The AutoTrans+RegControl decks are not of this class: r4133 never taps an AutoTrans, so it converges in 3 iterations because no control ever arms, and its state differs by 2.2-2.6 % at the regulated bus (cause regcontrol-autotrans-typecast).
causes.injection-fpc-delphi-ulp: Injection RHS entries a small factor above the calibrated faer-vs-KLU floor on IndMach-bearing asymmetric decks: transcendental last-ulp differences between the Delphi and FPC builds, amplified by the machine model (same class as the dSpeed cancellation floor). The injection assembly and the machine model are the same in r4088 and r4133.
causes.storage-display-precision: r4133 (a Delphi build) renders StorageController-dispatched Storage properties (.kw, %stored, kwhstored) to about 6 significant figures where this engine and dss_capi 0.14.5 return full f64: a Delphi-vs-FPC Format/Str last-digit rendering difference, not an operating-point move (the expected value rounded to 6 significant figures equals the actual one). This engine matches dss_capi 0.14.5. Ledgered as exact-pair property and probe entries (discrete state, never an envelope).
causes.pvsystem-display-precision: r4133 (a Delphi build) renders the PVSystem kvar/kva property to about 6 significant figures where this engine and dss_capi 0.14.5 return full f64: the same Delphi-vs-FPC Format/Str rendering difference as storage-display-precision, exact-pair only.
causes.property-format-brackets: The property system of dss_capi renders an array-valued PropertyValue with brackets ('[ 1900 1500 2300]') where r4133 returns it space-separated ('1900 1500 2300'): a property-rendering difference (dss_capi docs/known_differences.md). Exact-pair only.
causes.eventlog-trailing-space: r4133 writes a trailing space after relay and control event-log action text ('...LOCKED OUT '), which this engine, like dss_capi, trims. A whitespace rendering artifact on the diffing line only.
causes.harmonics-ieee519-r4133: Harmonics-mode node voltages on the IEEE_519 filter deck move between r4088 and r4133 (about 4.3e-4 at pcc) with the assembled Y bit-identical. The harmonics path is the same in both revisions, so the move is a build-to-build Delphi last-ulp drift amplified by the near-resonance of the 519 filter (an ill-conditioned harmonics fixpoint), not a behaviour change. This engine matches dss_capi 0.14.5.
causes.regcontrol-autotrans-typecast: The RegControl of r4133 reaches its controlled element through an unchecked cast to the Transformer class, while an AutoTrans is not a Transformer and its winding record stops matching the Transformer winding layout after Rdcohms. The tap increment therefore reads the winding's MaxTap (1.1 pu), and the pending tap change, Round(BoostNeeded/Increment)*Increment, rounds every realistic boost to zero, so r4133 never taps an AutoTrans: 0 event-log lines on all four controls:autotrans decks, and the regulated bus left below its band on every one of them (autotrans_reg: LOW.1/166 = 118.04 V against vreg=120 band=2, 0.96 V under the 119 V edge and 1.96 V under the setpoint, midi_autotrans: AT69.1/332 = 119.25 V against vreg=123 band=1.5, 3.00 V under the 122.25 V edge and 3.75 V under the setpoint) with 5-11 taps of headroom unused. Its winding currents and node voltages are those of the unregulated circuit (3-7.5 % on AutoTrans.WdgCurrents winding 2, 2.2-2.6 % at the regulated bus). Measured on the r4133 DLL through epri-worker: 'Edit AutoTrans.at wdg=2 maxtap=X' then '? RegControl.rat.tapnum' returns Round(puTap/maxtap) exactly (X=2.2 -> 0, X=1.1 -> 1, X=0.55 -> 2, where the correct answers are -14, 0, -25), 'tapnum=0' leaves taps=[1, 1.58101E-322], the winding's NumTaps=32 reinterpreted as a Double, forcing vreg=40 finally arms it and the event log reads 'CHANGED -1 TAPS TO 1.58101E-322', and the same four decks with the RegControl disabled make this engine print the census literals of r4133 byte for byte. Present identically in r3723, r4088 and r4133. dss_capi 0.14.5 does not have it (both classes share a controlled-transformer base). OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, so this engine keeps the regulated answer, pinned by props_r4133_pins::autotrans_wdgcurrents_stay_regulated_where_r4133_never_taps_the_autotrans. Reported to OpenDSS (the OpenDSS report 50-regcontrol-autotrans-ttransfobj-typecast.md). The bug rules out a conditioning reading of these decks: r4133 does not resolve the tap one step later, it never resolves one. No entry references this cause: the four decks gate on capi_v0145 only, so no r4133 comparison runs on them.
causes.makeposseq-fpc-delphi: MakePosSequence reduced parameters are quantized to five significant digits on r4133 and kept at full precision by dss_capi 0.14.5 and this engine: every MakePosSequence override of r4133 (Capacitor, Vsource, Load and Line alike) formats the reduced values into a command string with 5 significant digits and re-parses it, while dss_capi 0.14.5 aims typed setters at the same properties. Measured 2026-09-04 on modes:makeposseq/makeposseq_shunt.dss by a property census and a decomposition: the reduced kV reads 7.1996 on r4133 against 7.19955785679463 in this engine (rel 5.85e-06), load.kw 133.33 vs 133.333333333333 (2.50e-05), reactor.r 0.26667 vs 0.266666666666667 (1.25e-05). The quantized Vsource base kV alone moves the injection RHS by 3.407076218201843e-02 (rel 5.854e-06) with the cmatrix capacitor removed, while without the trailing makeposseq the two OpenDSS engines agree to f64-ulp (max 9.094947e-13, rel 1.563e-16). It is a value difference, not a transcendental last-ulp drift. No entry references this cause: the makeposseq decks gate on dss_capi 0.14.5, where the quantization does not exist, and modes:makeposseq/makeposseq_gic.dss gates on r4133 with every reduced parameter chosen so the 5-digit round trip is exact (basekv = 7.2*sqrt(3), kw=900, pf=1).
causes.reduce-fpc-delphi: Circuit reduction produces a different reduced network on r4133 than on dss_capi 0.14.5 and this engine: keep/merge/switch handling collapses branches differently, so a reduced Line YPrim can differ structurally and node voltages drift. This engine matches the reduced network of dss_capi 0.14.5 exactly, YPrim included.
causes.ckt24-regcontrol-conditioning: ckt24 substation RegControl/LDC tap current at the SubXFMR ultra-switch (a 1e-8 ohm stitch, Y about 1e8 S): the near-cancellation floors at rel about 1.2e-7, and last-ulp differences between the Delphi and FPC builds push the substation node voltage about 1.2x over the faer-vs-KLU-calibrated tolerance. A conditioning floor of the ultra-switch. This engine matches dss_capi 0.14.5.
causes.vsource-nearzero-power: Vsource power on an unenergized conductor, a near-zero common mode: r4133 reports exactly (0,0) on the floating conductor where this engine reports about 1e-4 VA (rel about 1e-7 on a 1 kV source), the near-ideal-source floating floor class. This engine matches dss_capi 0.14.5.
causes.monitor-seq-magnitude-drift: Sequence-magnitude monitor channel (V2, mode=32 sequence voltage) drifts above the 1e-6 monitor-channel abs floor: the symmetrical-component transform (Fortescue A-matrix over complex node voltages) amplifies transcendental last-ulp differences between the Delphi and FPC builds. This engine matches dss_capi 0.14.5, and the monitor code is the same in r4088 and r4133.
causes.gic-pct-r2-ignored: GICTransformer with winding 2 given by `%R`: both OpenDSS engines compute G2 = 100 / (ZBase2 * %R1), the G1 line copied with the base renamed and the percentage not, so a user's %R2 is stored and read back but never reaches the admittance. It is a slip, not a convention: the other arm of the same procedure restores %R2 from G2, and the forward and reverse maps are inverses of each other only when the forward one reads %R2. OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, so this engine reads %R2 in both lanes. These two decks are type=Auto, where the BusX side effect puts the G1 and G2 blocks in series on the H->X->neutral path, so the element admittance, the assembled Y, every node voltage and every element current differ from both OpenDSS engines (measured 2026-08-06 by the live corpus gate: node V 4.502e-4 V on gictransformer_gic against an allowed 1.001e-6, 1.021e-4 against 1.074e-6 on gic_midi, the tg3/tg5 YPrim block by 4/3). Correct value pinned by dss_core::exec::tests::compat_quirks::gic_transformer_pct_r2_drives_winding_two, which measures the %R path against the R1=/R2= ohms path, the arm neither engine gets wrong and which these decks also exercise (tg2/tg3, R1=0.2 R2=0.1). Report side: the value columns of tests/golden/reports/export_gicmvars are masked and pinned by golden_reports::export_gicmvars_matches_the_equivalent_ohms_spec. Props side: the R2 of the gictransformer_auto scenario is excluded in props_roundtrip::LANE_SKIP_SCENARIO_PROPS. The divergence class is any %R-specified GICTransformer: a deck writing only %R1= gives winding 2 the %R2 creation default 0.2 instead of repeating %R1. No corpus deck has that shape (the two decks above are the only %R decks and both set both), so only they are ledgered. Both decks gate on r4133 only, because dss_capi 0.14.5 is nondeterministic across processes on any deck that instantiates a GICTransformer. The pins named above read no OpenDSS engine.
causes.makeposseq-cuf-discarded: Capacitor MakePosSequence, cmatrix arm: the reduced capacitance is computed and then lost. dss_capi 0.14.5 aims the scalar setter at the array property Cuf, whose typed-setter tail handles only the three scalar double types and has no else arm, so the value is dropped with no error while the success path still marks the property set and runs the Cuf side effect (SpecType 2). The bank then computes from whatever capacitance it held (here the kvar=1200 kv=12.47 creation default, 20.4699706679377 uF), and the user's cmatrix is switched out of the YPrim for good. r4133 formats the same value into a command string, so it does apply it, but its cmatrix is already in farads while the cuf side effect multiplies the parsed array by 1.0e-6 again, landing 4e-12 F where its own 4e-6 F was meant. Neither engine produces the intended bank, and the intent is unambiguous because r4133 spells the array write out, so this engine performs it in both lanes in the property's own uF units. Capacitor.cap_cmat then holds 12 uF, the positive-sequence self term of its matrix (cause makeposseq-matrix-average-skips-the-first-row: the average of both OpenDSS engines is 4 uF, a third of it), where dss_capi keeps 20.47 uF. That moves the element's YPrim, the assembled Y, the node voltages (measured 2026-08-06 by the live corpus gate: 1.158e-1 V against an allowed 3.339e-6) and every element current. Correct value pinned by dss_core::elements::pd::capacitor::tests::make_pos_sequence_cmatrix_applies_the_positive_sequence_cuf, which asserts the reduced bank keeps the bank's power and has the YPrim of a phases=3 cuf=12 wye bank reduced beside it, and by ...::make_pos_sequence_cmatrix for the emitted action.
causes.makeposseq-matrix-average-skips-the-firs: MakePosSequence of a matrix-defined Capacitor (cmatrix) or Reactor (rmatrix/xmatrix): both OpenDSS engines average the mutual terms over rows 2..N with the diagonals 2..N in, so a balanced matrix reduces to (N-2)/N of its positive-sequence value -- one third at three conductors, zero at two, one half at four -- and a two-phase matrix reactor reduces to (M11 - M22)/2 of each matrix M, zero for equal diagonals (the solve turns NaN) and negative when the second diagonal is larger (an active element: rmatrix=[1|0.2 1.3] xmatrix=[10|1 12] writes R = -0.15, X = -1 and delivers 22.8 MW, where the matrix element draws 972.5 + j9922.3 kVA). Physics: under a balanced positive-sequence voltage an element of nodal matrix Y draws exactly 3 |V1|^2 conj(S(Y)) with S(Y) = (1/3) v1^H Y v1 = (sum_i Y_ii - sum_{i<j} Y_ij) / 3, and the positive-sequence circuit reports three times the one phase, so the reduced one-phase element must carry S of the matrix it stamps. The engine does that in both lanes: Cuf = S(C) for a cmatrix bank (12 uF for [10|-2 10|-2 -2 10], where the OpenDSS engines compute 4), R + jX = 1 / S((R + jX)^-1) for a series matrix reactor (0.8 + j9 for this deck's rx_mat, where they write 0.266666666666667 + j3 and the reduced reactor draws three times its power), R = 0, X = -1/S(B), Rp = 1/S(G) for Parallel=yes, and above three conductors the mean diagonal minus the mean off-diagonal term. Both OpenDSS engines share it, so no channel computes the right value. Pinned by dss_core::elements::pd::capacitor::tests::{make_pos_sequence_cmatrix, make_pos_sequence_cmatrix_applies_the_positive_sequence_cuf, make_pos_sequence_unbalanced_cmatrix_keeps_the_banks_power, make_pos_sequence_two_phase_cmatrix_keeps_the_banks_power, make_pos_sequence_four_conductor_cmatrix_takes_mean_self_minus_mean_mutual}, dss_core::elements::pd::reactor::tests::{make_pos_sequence_matrix, make_pos_sequence_matrix_shunt_keeps_the_reactors_power, make_pos_sequence_matrix_series_keeps_loss_and_load, make_pos_sequence_unbalanced_matrix_shunt_keeps_the_reactors_power, make_pos_sequence_parallel_matrix_keeps_the_reactors_power, make_pos_sequence_two_phase_matrix_keeps_the_reactors_power, make_pos_sequence_four_conductor_matrix_takes_mean_self_minus_mean_mutual}, dss_core::elements::pd::line::tests::{make_pos_sequence_matrix_branch, make_pos_sequence_two_phase_line_c1_is_the_shunt_self_term, make_pos_sequence_four_conductor_line_takes_mean_self_minus_mean_mutual}, dss_core::elements::pd::fault::tests::make_pos_sequence_gmatrix_fault_keeps_its_current and dss_core::exec::tests::make_pos_seq::makeposseq_shunt_reproduces_its_three_phase_solution.
causes.reactor-one-phase-z1-stamped-as-a-third: A one-phase Reactor given by symmetrical components (z1=, with z2/z0) stamps Z1/3 on both OpenDSS engines: the stamp takes Z1 as the one-phase diagonal and then divides every diagonal by 3, a division that belongs to the multi-phase (Z0 + Z1 + Z2)/3 only. So a native phases=1 z1=[1, 12] reactor draws exactly three times the power of its r=1 x=12 twin, and MakePosSequence of a three-phase Z1 reactor (a bare change to one phase) triples its power. Physics: a one-phase element with positive-sequence impedance Z1 has impedance Z1. The engine stamps Z1 in both lanes and divides by 3 only on the multi-phase diagonal, so the reduced three-phase reactor keeps its power (to the truncated-CALPHA floor of the three-phase stamp, about 2e-7). No corpus deck declares a one-phase Z1 reactor, so the reduced rx_z1 of modes:makeposseq/makeposseq_shunt.dss is the one observable compared with an OpenDSS engine. Pinned by dss_core::elements::pd::reactor::tests::a_single_phase_z1_reactor_stamps_z1 and dss_core::exec::tests::make_pos_seq::makeposseq_shunt_reproduces_its_three_phase_solution.
causes.mmf-text-accept-set: LoadShape memory-mapped plain-text reader: both OpenDSS engines filter each comma-delimited column through an accept-set of bytes in [46,58), '.' (46), '/' (47) and the digits (48-57). That deletes the sign (45), '+' (43), the exponent letter e/E (101/69) and whitespace while keeping '/' inside the token, so -0.5 reads as 0.5 and 1.5e-3 as 1.53. It is a slip in the mapped reader, not a second file format: a LoadShape owns a second reader for the same file, the non-mapped CSV reader, which hands each row to the aux parser, and MemoryMapping=Yes selects how a shape is stored, not what its bytes mean, so the two must agree on identical input. This engine takes the column verbatim through that same parser in both lanes. shape_mmf.dss exists to observe the slip (its mmpq8.csv P column is written in exponent notation on purpose), so ls_pq reads {0.15, 0.20, ...} instead of {1.51, 2.01, ...} and the deck differs wholesale from dss_capi (measured 2026-08-06 by the live corpus gate: node V 1.641e1 V against an allowed 8.179e-6, with Load.ld_pq's YPrim, the assembled Y, the injection RHS, every element channel and all four monitors following). Correct values pinned by dss_core::elements::general::load_shape::tests::mmf_text_reader_agrees_with_its_non_mapped_twin and ...::mmf_plaintext_reader_keeps_sign_and_exponent. The other coverage of the deck (the sngfile=/dblfile= MMF readers, the raw mult=(sngfile=) directive form, the pqcsvfile= two-column reader, the array-property round-trip and the Set/Get totaltime surface) lives in the sibling deck modes:inputformat/shape_mmf_io/shape_mmf_io.dss, which gates clean on the same channel. That exactly one deck can see the fix is measured in bytes by ...::mmf_accept_set_fix_is_gated_by_exactly_one_deck.
causes.epri-303-crash: r4133 raises a #303/#58614 access violation on this deck (binary/MMF GrowthShape, line/cable spacing, or the CapControl Type=Follow ControlSignal feature) where this engine and dss_capi 0.14.5 solve it, so the r4133 channel cannot compare it. The capi_v0145 channel gates the deck fully.
causes.epri-espvlcontrol-uninstantiable: The r4133 DLL (Version 11.0.0.1) cannot instantiate class ESPVLControl at all: every `New espvlcontrol.<name>` raises #303 'Access violation ... Read of address 0x0' before any property is parsed. Measured 2026-08-29 through epri-worker on a minimal deck (`clear; New circuit.min basekv=12.47 phases=3 bus1=src; New espvlcontrol.a` -> AV at offset 8F3F2D reading 0x70, and with `element=line.l1 terminal=1` on a two-bus feeder -> AV at offset 15440 reading 0x0). It is not deck-specific: dss_capi 0.14.5 and this engine both build the class and sample it, so the capi_v0145 channel gates the deck fully while the r4133 channel is skipped. On dss_capi a SystemController redispatch corrupts the process (its type-confused `Gen.kWBase` store), so the deck keeps that redispatch silent (the case's manifest note). A candidate for an OpenDSS report.
causes.ncim-oppoint: NCIM (Newton current injection) is a solver dss_capi 0.14.5 lacks (Set algorithm=NCIM is ignored, Export deltaf raises #24713), so only the r4133 channel gates an NCIM deck. The four NCIM decks (modes ncim_pq/ncim_pv_pq/ncim_midi and solvable_now Xmission_System_Kundur2Area) are live-gated on r4133 with no ledger entry: the whole-model compare (node V, system Y, the Vsource swing current/power/loss, the NCIM generators and the warm-resolve iteration count) is within the tier floor on every case (measured 2026-07-20 by epri-worker probes of r4133 'Version 11.0.0.1 (64-bit build)'). Converged node voltages agree with r4133 digit for digit (about 1e-12, faer vs KLU), and the reported current of the swing source matches r4133 to the floor. That current is solution::solution::ncim::ncim_stamp_swing_source_currents, stamped into the source's terminal currents at the end of the NCIM solution and returned by the NCIM arm of the Vsource, so one live state feeds the gate reader and the element path alike. Its PC term subtracts where r4133 adds: the addition is an OpenDSS KCL sign bug, measured 2026-09-03 on a deck with a load bonded onto the swing bus and not reproduced in either lane (pin ncim_swing_sum_subtracts_pc_terminals_and_closes_kcl). It is unreachable on every gated NCIM case, none of which carries a PC element on the swing bus (pin ncim_swing_bus_carries_no_pc_element_on_the_gated_decks). Warm-resolve iterations match r4133 exactly (2/2/2 on the modes decks, 1 on Kundur2Area). No entry references this cause (see exec::tests::ncim).
causes.gfm-pctstored-rounding: Grid-forming (GFM) storage decks: the solved model matches r4133 (this engine takes the Isc1 default of r4133) except the Storage.%stored getter string, which r4133 rounds to about 4-6 decimals (92.4321) where this engine and dss_capi return full f64 (92.4320641163609), a getter rendering difference, exact-pair only. The capi_v0145 channel cannot gate these decks: the different Isc1 default of 0.14.5 makes the assembled system Y differ wholesale (x1000), a model default this engine takes from r4133.
causes.regcontrol-idle: RegControl `idle` is a feature dss_capi 0.14.5 rejects (#110 Unknown parameter 'idle'), so only the r4133 channel gates the idle-regulator deck. A regulator idles when the through-power lies inside the bounded [RevPowerThreshold, FwdPowerThreshold] band, both bounds at once, as r4133 computes it. dss_capi 0.15.x writes the test as an OR, a tautology under the default symmetric band that keeps an idling regulator from ever tapping (MV.1 8.8 % low). With the bounded test the idle tap and voltage match r4133 exactly (tapnum 15, tap 1.09375, MV.1 = 7650.08 V), and widening fwdThreshold to bracket the load makes r4133 idle to 7030.24 V, which shows the bounded mechanism (measured 2026-07-19 through epri-worker). The only residual is a getter convention on revThreshold/fwdThreshold: the getter of r4133 returns the default display strings (revThreshold '100', the band half-width, fwdThreshold unset '') decoupled from the signed internal, while this engine reports the signed effective thresholds in kW (rev -100, fwd +100). Definitional, not physics, so exact-pair.
causes.linespacing-normamps: Line built from LineSpacing+wiredata: dss_capi 0.14.5 reports Line.lsp.normamps=730/emergamps=1095, the NormAmps of the first wire (ACSR_556), where this engine and r4133 report 230/345, the minimum NormAmps over the phase conductors (min{556->730, 4-0->340, 1-0->230} = 230). The weakest phase conductor bounds the line (cause geometry-weakest-phase), so on capi_v0145 this engine diverges from 0.14.5 on purpose (measured 2026-07-18 by the corpus gate: this engine 230/345, dss_capi 0.14.5 730/1095). r4133 #303-crashes this deck (skip). Exact-pair property entry on capi_v0145.
causes.generator-makeposseq-foreign-slots: The Generator MakePosSequence of dss_capi 0.14.5 decides 'the user set kVA=/MVA=' from the raw property-sequence slots 26/27, but its property order puts Xdp/Xdpp at 26/27 and kVA/MVA at 23/24, so both rating guards read foreign cells: a 3-phase generator declared with kVA=/MVA= keeps its full rating after makeposseq instead of having it divided by the phase count. r4133 reads the same two slots, and there they hold kVA and MVA, so the defect is dss_capi's. This engine divides the rating in both lanes, as r4133 does, and dss_capi 0.14.5 keeps the undivided value. Exact-pair (a discrete value jump, not display precision).
causes.makeposseq-runs-again-on-a-reduced-circu: MakePosSequence on a circuit already positive-sequence reduces it again on both OpenDSS engines: a Load's kW, kvar and xfkVA are divided by 3 a second time and every Vsource's BasekV by sqrt(3) a second time, so a 400 kW load reads kW 44.44, a ninth, and on dss_capi draws 46.02 kW at 0.58 pu (measured 2026-10-23 with the pinned dss-python on makeposseq_pc_repeat.dss), and the source EMF falls to 12.47/3 kV. This engine changes nothing on a positive-sequence circuit (the CktModel guard of exec::make_pos_seq), so after a second makeposseq it holds the circuit of the first: the one-phase equivalent of a reduced circuit is that circuit.
causes.line-merge-length-units-reset: Line merge of a matrix-model series branch and its length units. r4133 saves the units before the merge and re-applies them with a separate edit that runs after the rmatrix/xmatrix and cmatrix edits, because the matrix side effect resets the length units. Its MakePosSequence repeats the units for the same reason. dss_capi 0.14.5 inverts the two: it writes the length and the units as fields and then runs the rmatrix/xmatrix/cmatrix side effects, whose units reset wipes the units back to none one statement later, so every matrix-model series merge on 0.14.5 reports 'none'. OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, so this engine keeps the saved units in both lanes and the three merged lines of this deck render their saved 'kft'. Probed 2026-08-28 on the r4133 DLL (Version 11.0.0.1, tools/opendss/bin/r4133): 'kft' on all three merged lines here, and deck-dependent elsewhere ('mi'/'cm' on two purpose-built micro-decks, 'none' on a switch), so the getter is live state and not an echo. The electrical model does not move: the unit conversion returns 1.0 whenever either side is none, so the conversion factor is 1.0 on both engines either way, and the merged line's YPrim, the assembled Y, the node voltages, currents, powers, losses, the node count (88) and the iteration count (5) are identical on all three engines. The same lost units make the EnergyMeter zone walk of dss_capi read the merged 4 kft lines as 4 km, so its Bus.Distance is 4.0 km high at l2e, l3e and l9e (entry reduce-merge-units-lost-midi-capi-distance). Correct value pinned by dss_core::exec::tests::reduce::merged_matrix_line_keeps_the_surviving_lines_length_units, which reads two micro-decks whose surviving lines carry different saved units (so the pin cannot pass against a hardwired getter) plus an un-merged control and a post-merge rmatrix= reset.
causes.line-switch-kills-linecode: Line switch= and the LineCode flag. r4133 keeps two pieces of state, the linecode-specified flag and the code name, both set when a LineCode is fetched. The impedance side effects clear the flag, but the switch= side effect does not: it sets the switch impedances and length 0.001 and resets the length units, and leaves the flag alone, an omission written arm by arm beside the two arms that do clear it. The flag is read live by the linecode getter (the code name when set, '' otherwise), so it is not an echo of the stored property text, and by the units= side effect, which converts from the units of the LineCode when the flag is set and from the line's own when it is not. dss_capi 0.14.5 adds a kill of the flag to the switch= arm. OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, and a switch= keeps the LineCode the user named, so this engine keeps the flag on switch= in both lanes. r4133 clears the flag in eight other places (the two impedance arms and the spacing, conductor, wire, CN cable, TS cable and geometry fetches), and this engine has a counterpart for each of them: a probe of the r4133 DLL on 2026-08-29 measured '? Line.<x>.linecode' = '' behind a 'conductors=[..]'. No impedance moves on this corpus: every one of the five cells declares units=m on the LineCode and on the Line, so both branches compute a conversion of 1.0. Measured 2026-08-29 on all three engines: r1 = '1' on r4133, on dss_capi 0.14.5 and in this engine, node voltages agreeing to 1.1e-10 relative, and the r4133-vs-engine current spread (9.7e-08) smaller than the capi-vs-engine spread (1.9e-07) on the same deck, the faer-vs-KLU near-cancellation floor on an ideal switch, not a flag effect. The consequence of the flag is pinned on a purpose-built discriminating deck (a code in kft, the line in m, where the two branches differ by 304.8) by exec::tests::line_fetch::switch_yes_keeps_the_linecode_and_its_units_conversion, in both lanes and without an OpenDSS engine, through the rendered r1 and through the solved node voltages of that deck, pinned against the YNodeVarray of r4133 (the flagged switch drops 1/304.8 of what the identical bare switch drops). The r4133 channel needs no entry: these five cells compare and match there.
causes.swtcontrol-per-phase-state-render: The switch state of a SwtControl is per phase on r4133 and scalar on dss_capi 0.14.5, so the two engines render different shapes for the same state. r4133 holds the present and normal states one slot per phase (every slot closed at creation), written ganged from a bare token or phase by phase from a quoted list (first-character match, at most 5 tokens), each slot driving its own conductor and re-applied per phase. Its getters render one token per controlled-element phase in the '[tok, tok, ... ]' form for Normal and State, and '[]' when the controlled element is nil. dss_capi 0.14.5 has no per-phase model (one value per object), so it renders the bare word 'closed'/'open'. A switch opens and closes per conductor, so this engine keeps the per-phase model in both lanes, and every SwtControl Normal/State cell on the 0.14.5 channel is a rendering-shape divergence with the identical switch state behind it: the tokens of this engine are exactly the word of dss_capi, repeated once per controlled phase. Structural only: no conductor, YPrim, node voltage, current, power, loss or iteration count moves, and Lock/Action/Delay/SwitchedObj are untouched (the census reports no other moved cell on any of the five cases). Measured 2026-09-02 on the r4133 DLL (Version 11.0.0.1, tools/opendss/bin/r4133) over all five gated decks: swtcontrol_lock '[closed, closed, closed, ]' for Normal and State both before and after the locked post 'action=open', makeposseq_ctrl '[closed, ]' for both (the switched line is 1-phase after MakePosSequence), and each IEEE_519 copy '[closed, closed, closed, ]' for both of its two controls, byte-identical to what this engine renders. The r4133 channel needs no entry: the 80 in-scope cells of the pair (swtcontrol.normal and swtcontrol.state, 40 each, on the three r4133-gating decks midi_swtcontrol, swtcontrol_time and civanlar) compare and match, measured 2026-09-02 with the property census (DSS_PROPS_CENSUS), which reports zero Normal/State rows on that channel and leaves only pairs other causes own (Delay, Action, Reset, SwitchedObj, enabled). Correct value pinned by dss_core::exec::tests::controls::swtcontrol_state_renders_one_token_per_controlled_phase (the gated decks plus the 1/2/3-phase discriminator) and dss_core::exec::tests::controls::swtcontrol_state_renders_per_phase_on_the_r4133_only_decks (the three in-scope decks, which no capi channel can witness because 0.14.5 cannot render the array).
causes.swtcontrol-delay-not-wired: r4133 never wires SwtControl property 5 `Delay`: its edit handler has no arm for it, so `delay=` lands only in the stored property text while the time delay keeps its creation value 120.0, and the live getter renders that (to 7 significant digits). dss_capi 0.14.5 wires the property to the time delay and this engine does too, so a deck that sets `delay=` reads back its own value here and 120 there. The divergence is render-only on r4133: nothing consumes the time delay there (the queue-pushing body of its sample step and its pending-action handler are commented out, and the state setter acts immediately), and the event log and control queue of the two decks are empty under r4133 and live-compared. OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, so this engine keeps the property wired, and the bug is reported (the OpenDSS report 43-swtcontrol-delay-not-wired.md), excluded here and pinned by the expected-value pins named in `source`. Exact-pair (a discrete value jump, not display precision).
causes.windgen-kvar-renders-dispatched-q: r4133 renders WindGen property 11 `kvar` from the dispatched reactive power instead of the base kvar the property documents: its getter formats the present kvar, which returns the nominal per-phase Q times the phase count. The edit arm exists and stores the value in the base kvar, so this is not an echo: probed on r4133 through epri-worker, a deck typing `kvar=500` renders `0`, and after `Edit kvar=777` the render is still `0` while `? PF` renders 0.968058 (= 3000/sqrt(3000^2+777^2)), so the value is parsed and the getter reports a different live field. The rendered zero on these decks comes from a second, independent OpenDSS bug (cause windgen-qmode0-no-arm): the steady-state QMode dispatch has no arm for the default QMode 0 and zeroes the dispatch. The render is wrong independently of it: with QMode=1 the same deck renders 363.54 for a typed kvar=500 (the operating-point Q), and in dynamics, where the Q block is skipped, it renders the intermediate 777 while the base kvar is 792.718441186736 and the measured terminal Q is -37087.76 kvar. The sibling class settles it inside the same engine: the Generator of r4133 has the identical present-kvar getter and the identical property help, yet renders the base kvar. Consequence beyond the API: Save Circuit writes the property text through this getter, so it writes `kvar=0` for a machine built with kvar=500 (produced on r4133), and the reload resets PFNominal to 1.0 and kvarMax/kvarMin to 0, a silent model corruption. dss_capi 0.14.5 has no WindGen class, so there is no second witness. This engine renders the base kvar, as its Generator and the Generator of r4133 do. OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, so the bug is reported (the OpenDSS report 44-windgen-kvar-renders-dispatched-q.md), excluded here and pinned by the expected-value pins named in `source`. This render pair is independent of the dispatch: r4133 renders the dispatched Q, this engine renders the base kvar, and the dispatch never writes the base kvar. Exact-pair (a discrete value jump, not display precision).
causes.windgen-qmode0-no-arm: WindGen steady-state QMode dispatch: r4133 implements QMode 1 (PF) and QMode 2 (volt-var) and has no arm for QMode 0, so its fallback zeroes the reactive dispatch, while QMode defaults to 0, the property help documents it as 'Q control mode (0:Q, 1:PF, 2:VV)', and the dynamics model implements 0 as constant Q (Qord = Qref). A default-configured WindGen therefore injects zero vars in power flow however its kvar=/pf= reads. It is an omission, not a design: the same engine dispatches the base kvar whenever the QMode case is bypassed (model=4, constant-Q generation: probed terminal Q -726.4287342535065 kvar on windgen_snap_delta and -985.9891404764404 on windgen_daily), the saturation fallback of arm 1 is the base kvar, arm 2 is the base kvar scaled by the VV curve and saturated at |kvarBase| (probed: a flat y=+1 curve dispatches exactly the base), and the parent Generator class writes the dispatch outright. Probed 2026-09-04 on the r4133 DLL (Version 11.0.0.1): QMode=0 dispatches exactly 0 on all five decks and in every configuration, including decks that type kvar=, pf= and kVA=, `edit QMode=0` is inert, and no other code path fills the nominal Q for mode 0. OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, so this engine dispatches kvarCalc = kvarBase for QMode 0 in both lanes (elements::pc::windgen::nominal), read raw where kVA= is unset (the sign of the pf convention is already in the base there) and as |kvarBase| with LeadLag = -1 for PFNominal < 0 where a typed kVA= has stripped that sign, the discipline of arm 1. No kVArating clamp applies, because the saturation test of arm 1 cannot fire: kVATmp = sqrt(Pg^2 + kvarCalc^2) is Pg/|PF| and Pg is capped at kWBase, so kVATmp <= kWBase/|PF| == kVArating bit for bit (measured on 3000/0.95, 1584/0.88, 1080/0.9). The sign comes from PFNominal and not from the base alone: with kVA= set the base is re-derived as sqrt(kVArating^2 - kWBase^2), a non-negative root that strips the sign a typed pf<0 or kvar<0 put there, so reading the base raw would dispatch the opposite sign from arm 1 on identical tokens. Probed on r4133 for kW=1000 kVA=1200 pf=-0.9: arm 1 gives terminal Q +523.0678462465884 kvar (the machine absorbs, which is what pf<0 means), while model=4 of r4133, reading the stripped base, gives -523.0475290915948 (injecting), and mode 0 of this engine follows arm 1. With kVA= unset the two formulations are bit-identical. The generation multiplier still applies (probed: Set genmult=0.5 halves it). The dispatch feeds Yeq, so it moves every GenModel that reads Yeq: model 1 (the only one any modes:windgen deck declares), model 2 and the model-6 YPrim seed, while models 4/5 read varBase and are untouched. The four decks that declare a WindGen without a QMode= token therefore diverge from r4133 across the solved model. The fifth, modes:windgen/windgen_snap.dss, types pf=1.0, so its base kvar is 0 and the arm is a no-op there (measured: that case stays fully compared and green and has no entry). Correct values pinned by dss_core::elements::pc::windgen::tests::qmode0_dispatches_the_base_kvar, ::qmode0_dispatch_carries_the_sign_and_scales_with_genmult and ::qmode0_zero_only_when_the_base_is_zero, which name both engines' numbers, and the dynamics state by ::dynamics_variables_match_the_qmode0_dispatch. Reported to OpenDSS (the OpenDSS report 55-windgen-qmode0-zero-var-dispatch.md). The property side is separate: the kvar getter of r4133 renders the dispatched Q (cause windgen-kvar-renders-dispatched-q) and this engine renders the base kvar, which this dispatch never writes, so the four r4133-windgen-kvar-dispatched-* property entries keep their pairs.
causes.capcontrol-time-bus-is-the-capacitors: CapControl TIMECONTROL, the bus of terminal 1: r4133 requires a monitored element for every control type except FOLLOWCONTROL and binds the control's own bus 1 to that element's terminal. Its fallback to bus 1 of the controlled element is the no-monitored-element arm only. dss_capi 0.14.5, for TIMECONTROL and FOLLOWCONTROL, takes the controlled element and forces terminal 1, so its bus 1 is the capacitor's bus. This engine binds the terminal of the monitored element, the bus the control is declared to watch, as r4133 does (elements::control::cap_control, the `control_type != Follow` arm). The `VoltagesMagAng` channel makes the bus observable, because the field reads NodeV through the element's own NodeRef. So on a `type=time element=...` CapControl the capi_v0145 channel reports the voltage of the capacitor's bus and this engine, as r4133, the voltage of the monitored element's terminal: a different bus, not a numeric gap. The r4133 channel of the same case compares clean and needs no entry. Both numbers pinned by dss_core::exec::tests::derived_polar::capcontrol_time_voltages_follow_the_monitored_elements_terminal.
causes.posseq-seqpowers-slot-stride: CktElement.SeqPowers of r4133 writes the 1-phase positive-sequence arm into the wrong slot with the wrong stride: it carries the one-based start and step of the sequence-current helper onto a zero-based array and then keeps a stride of one, so the positive-sequence power of terminal t lands in flat slot t+2 (terminal 1 in the negative-sequence slot, terminal 2 in the zero-sequence slot of the next terminal, and so on) instead of 3t+1. dss_capi 0.14.5 is right on the same arm, and so are the four sequence helpers of both engines. SeqCurrents and SeqVoltages go through those helpers, so the divergence is seq_powers only. OpenDSS bugs are never reproduced, so this engine emits the layout of dss_capi. Reported to OpenDSS (the OpenDSS report 67-seqpowers-posseq-slot-stride.md).
causes.visualize-dssview-file-pair: `Visualize <quantity> <element>` writes a DSSView file pair on r4133 and nothing on dss_capi 0.14.5, so a deck that issues it diverges on the created-file set of the r4133 channel only. r4133 builds <output dir>/<circuit>_<class>_<name>_PQ.DSV (_V.DSV and _I.DSV for the other two quantities), writes that text file and then creates its binary companion with the .dbl extension, one pair per DSSView viewer artifact. dss_capi 0.14.5 instead assembles a JSON object {PlotType: 'Visualize', ElementName, ElementType, Quantity} and hands it to the plot callback, opening no file (a no-op under a headless NIL callback). This engine follows the JSON payload (exec::plot, fire_visualize_callback): a headless engine has no DSSView to feed, and a callback payload is the interface a client can consume, where a .DSV/.dbl pair is a Windows-viewer file format. A deliberate product divergence, not an OpenDSS bug, so no OpenDSS report is owed, and it costs exactly the two r4133-only names.
causes.di-hourly-reactive-energy-cancels: The hourly net reactive energy of the ckt7 feeder is a near-cancellation: the EnergyMeter integrates the kvar of every zone element over the hour, and on the 24 cells this cause covers the capacitive and inductive halves of the feeder cancel to |kvarh| <= 76.7594 in this engine (<= 76.7674 including both OpenDSS engines) while the real-energy register of the same row is kWh >= 2106.0996, so the summands are 46.376x .. 11031.672x the net they add up to. Three measured facts make the residual an indeterminate rather than a bug of this engine. (a) The cancellation above. (b) The residual is inside the accumulator's own class on its uncancelled twin: the absolute gap of this engine is at most 8.010487e-03 kvarh, at most 0.023012 of the energy band the kWh of the same row earns (a band never narrower than 0.2107), equivalently 5.4927e-08 .. 1.6014e-06 of the row's own Max kVA, the i_rel(large) = 1e-6 scale of the powers being integrated, exceeded by at most 1.6014x and only on 2 of the 24 cells (Time 475 on r4133, Time 478 on both). (c) No engine-independent value exists at that scale: the two KLU-based OpenDSS engines disagree with each other by 2.443741e-05 .. 2.513225e-03 kvarh = 2.7 % .. 88.8 % of the gap of this engine on the same cell, and exceed the energy class between themselves on 6 of the 24 cells (Times 359, 477, 827, 850, 2596, 8517), worst ratio 4.021 at Time 359 (capi 1.01464560883437 vs r4133 1.01383583996829). The larger faer perturbation of this engine only scales an indeterminacy the two KLU engines already have between themselves. Widening the energy band to admit these cells would widen every energy cell on a `large` deck by about 5e-3 kvarh (50x the class's own `abs`) to admit 20, and a tolerance is never loosened to make a comparison pass. Measured 2026-09-11 by a five-case drive of both transports at the gate's own capture slot, re-derived per cell at full precision 2026-09-12. Pinned by di_pins::the_ckt7_hourly_kvarh_is_a_cross_engine_indeterminate.
causes.di-voltexception-argmin-tie: The `Min LV Bus` column of the voltage-exception report is the argmin of a tied minimum on ckt7. The report scans the buses in list order and keeps the first strict minimizer (Vmagpu below the running minimum), and the scan of this engine does the same (same order, same strict `<`, same `> 0.1` neutral guard, same kVBase split). On ckt7 the three service buses s1x_1001577 / s2x_1001577 / s3x_1001577 carry the same node magnitudes bit for bit in the OpenDSS solution (0x1.c26d89b2b06a6p-1, 0x1.c5736ad8e99ddp-1, 0x1.c69388d539fa3p-1 at each of the three), so the minimum is attained at three buses at once, and which one a strict `<` scan reports is decided by the last bit of the solve: the faer solution of this engine breaks the tie at s2x_1001577 / s3x_1001577 where both KLU-based OpenDSS engines break it at s1x_1001577. Each of the three is a correct answer, and the value column `Min LV Voltage` agrees inside the voltage class on all 7316 rows, so the name column carries no information the value column does not. `Min Bus`, `Max Bus` and `Max LV Bus` stay compared and match on every row of every case. Measured 2026-09-11 by the same drive as di-hourly-reactive-energy-cancels.
causes.geometry-weakest-phase: A LineGeometry rating nobody typed is the weakest phase conductor's, and so is the rating of a Line on it, where both OpenDSS engines copy conductor 1's. Every phase conductor carries the line current and every loading reader compares the largest phase current with the Line's one rating, so the weakest phase conductor's rating is the largest single rating that never misses an overload (not the exact check of each phase current against its own conductor, which no reader makes). The spacing form already reads it so on the engine and on r4133. The asymmetric geometry oh3 (ACSR_336_4 530 A, ACSR_4-0 340 A, ACSR_1-0 230 A on the phases, emergency ratings 1.5 times) reads 230/345 where both OpenDSS engines read 530/795. Pinned by exec::tests::ratings::a_geometry_line_is_rated_by_its_weakest_phase_conductor.
causes.two-winding-kva-derives-the-kva-ratings: A kVA typed at the second winding of a two-winding Transformer, AutoTrans or XfmrCode is the kVA of both windings, and the documentation defaults NormHkVA and EmergHkVA to 110 % and 150 % of winding 1's kVA. The engine derives both kVA ratings from that kVA, as a kVA typed at winding 1 does, while both OpenDSS engines keep the ratings of the kVA winding 1 held before, so a unit is rated for a kVA it no longer has. Measured 2026-10-25 with the epri-worker on the r4133 DLL and on the pinned dss-python: wdg=2 kva=1000 on a 500 kVA two-winding unit reads NormHkVA 550 and EmergHkVA 750 on both, wdg=1 kva=1000 reads 1100 and 1500. Reported to OpenDSS.
causes.storage-charges-at-the-efficiency-of-its: A Storage charging through an EffCurve stores the AC power times the efficiency the curve gives at the per-unit DC power, P = eta(P / kVA) P_ac, solved on the curve segment that holds it. Both OpenDSS engines solve it by trial and, when the segment of the AC power is not the segment of the DC power, apply the second segment's efficiency to the DC power of the first pass instead of to the AC power, so the efficiency is applied twice and less energy is stored than the curve allows. Measured 2026-10-25 with the epri-worker on the r4133 DLL and on the pinned dss-python: one charging hour at 100 kW on xarray=[0 0.8 1.2] yarray=[0.9 0.9 0.5] (kVA 120, 2000 kWh stored) stores 2074.21111404038 kWh on dss_capi and 2074.21 on r4133, the flat 0.9 curve 2080.10400007158 on both, the value the engine stores for either. Reported to OpenDSS.
causes.vccs-rms-seed-filter-at-rest: Both OpenDSS engines seed the input history of the RMS VCCS filter with the RMS voltage, where the filter's input is the current command, so their filter starts out of rest. The engine starts it at rest at the seeded current. An RMS VCCS therefore leaves its seed on another trajectory until the history has decayed, and with it the node voltage a dynamics run saves at its last Y rebuild, which the bus `Voc` reads, while the final node voltages agree. Pinned by exec::tests::dynamics_membership::joining::a_vccs_holds_its_operating_point_at_any_sample_rate and by the pre-fault filter output of exec::tests::vccs::vccs_rmsmode_dynamics_mode3_matches_oracle_1phase and ::vccs_rmsmode_dynamics_mode3_matches_oracle_3phase.

entries.source: Measured 2026-09-05 by the live corpus gate and by a one-shot epri-worker probe (r4133 DLL Version 11.0.0.1): this deck is the only corpus case that puts the 1-phase positive-sequence arm on the r4133 channel. Both numbers, flat (re, im) kVA in each engine's own layout: Vsource.source this engine [1] (-14353.237123021707, -23926.665217436668) vs r4133 [2] (-14353.237123021703, -23926.66521743667), Line.feed this engine [1] (14353.237123021703, 23926.665217436665) and [4] (-4782.567248087438, 1.7462298274040223e-13) vs r4133 [2] and [3], GICTransformer.gt this engine [1] (4779.801159453495, 0.0) vs r4133 [2], Load.ld1 this engine [1] (2.7660886339429944, -1.7053025658242405e-16) vs r4133 [2]. seq_currents and seq_voltages agree on this deck within the micro floor and stay compared, which is why the scope names seq_powers and nothing else. Pinned on this deck by `the_gic_posseq_deck_keeps_every_terminal_power_in_its_positive_slot` (exec::tests::derived_seq), which carries the numbers of both layouts, and the population of that arm is re-derived every run by `harness::assert_seq_arm_population` (SEQ_ARM_CENSUS_MEASURED.2 = 4). Scope: the `kvarh` column of the two files that carry it on this deck, example_ckt7/di_yr_0/di_totals_1.csv and .../25607_1.csv (one meter, so the totals file mirrors the meter file). 20 cells of 8760 rows x 68 columns per file fail the energy class on this channel (17 on the other one, 24 in the union, which is the set the cause and the pin quantify). Both numbers at the three rows the pin names, this engine vs capi_v0145: row 352 7.21266169258719 vs 7.2086109009058 (ratio 4.935), row 477 0.412764282391174 vs 0.41082760865509 (ratio 13.727, the worst cell of this channel, 16.845 on r4133), row 478 -76.7593383203749 vs -76.7673488074516 (the largest absolute gap of the surface, 8.010487e-03 kvarh). (c) The two OpenDSS engines disagree with each other by 2.7 % .. 88.8 % of that gap and exceed the energy class between themselves on 6 of the 24 cells, worst 4.021x at Time 359. Two stronger claims fail on this data: |capi - r4133| exceeds the class on 6 of the 24 cells, not on every one, and the gap of this engine stays under i_rel(large) x Max kVA on 22 of the 24.
